$comment: SEED CORPUS — India. Read data/README.md before adding an entry. Two rules govern this file and nothing overrides them: (1) every statement is a real, publicly-reported, on-record remark by a public figure acting in a public role, carrying at least one live source link; (2) nothing here is paraphrased into the `quote` field — if the exact wording could not be established from a source, `quote` is null and `claim` carries a neutral summary instead. `stage` is the content-pipeline stage each entry has actually cleared (docs/03-content-pipeline.md §3.3). No entry in this file has cleared Stage 3; none is publishable as-is.

statements.neutral_title: On cloud cover and radar
statements.quote: लेकिन मैंने कहा कि बादल और बारिश से फायदा भी है। हम रडार से बच सकते हैं।
statements.quote_translation: But I said that clouds and rain also have an advantage. We can evade radar.
statements.quote_note: Original Hindi as quoted in ThePrint Hindi's report of the News Nation interview. The full interview still needs audiovisual timestamps and surrounding context.
statements.claim: That cloud cover would reduce the chance of Indian aircraft being detected by Pakistani radar during the Balakot operation.
statements.context: Modi described overruling expert hesitation on the night of the strike, calling the reasoning his 'raw wisdom'. The full interview is the context that must be captured before publication; the surrounding minutes are about the decision to proceed in poor weather.
statements.counterpoint: Radar operates at wavelengths that pass through cloud largely unattenuated; cloud affects visual and some electro-optical targeting, not radar detection.

surrounding 60 seconds transcribed and reviewed

statements.neutral_title: On Ganesha, Karna and the antiquity of surgery
statements.quote: महाभारत का कहना है कि कर्ण मां की गोद से पैदा नहीं हुआ था, इसका मतलब ये हुआ कि उस समय Genetic Science मौजूद था। तभी तो कर्ण, मां की गोद के बिना उसका जन्म हुआ होगा। हम गणेश जी की पूजा करते हैं, कोई तो प्लास्टिक सर्जन होगा उस जमाने में, जिसने मनुष्य के शरीर पर हाथी का सर रख कर के प्लास्टिक सर्जरी का प्रारंभ हुआ होगा।
statements.quote_translation: The Mahabharata says that Karna was not born from his mother's womb; this means genetic science existed at that time. That is how Karna could have been born without his mother's womb. We worship Lord Ganesha; there must have been a plastic surgeon in those days who put an elephant's head on a human body and began plastic surgery.
statements.quote_note: Original Hindi from the speaker's published transcript. An invisible Unicode joiner in “प्लास्टिक” was normalized; official audiovisual footage and audience reaction remain outstanding.
statements.claim: That reproductive genetics and plastic surgery were practised in ancient India, evidenced by episodes in the Mahabharata and by the iconography of Ganesha.
statements.context: Said to an audience of doctors and medical scientists while opening a hospital.
statements.policy_note: Borderline under Rule 1 (religion). Committee ruling: IN SCOPE. The claim under review is a claim about the history of medicine, made to doctors, in a hospital. The archive takes no position on the epics or on anyone's faith, and the entry must never be titled or captioned in a way that implies otherwise.

statements.neutral_title: On whether evolution was witnessed
statements.quote: ना तो हमारे पूर्वजों ने और ना ही किसी और ने कभी यह कहा या लिखा कि उन्होंने किसी बंदर को इंसान में परिवर्तित होते देखा।
statements.quote_translation: Neither our ancestors nor anyone else ever said or wrote that they had seen an ape turn into a human.
statements.quote_note: Original Hindi quoted by Aaj Tak and corroborated by NDTV's contemporaneous video page. A full event recording with surrounding context remains outstanding.
statements.claim: That the theory of evolution is scientifically wrong and should be removed from school and university curricula, because no eyewitness account exists of an ape becoming a man.
statements.context: Singh, a former Mumbai Police Commissioner, was then a junior minister for education. He repeated the position several times over the following weeks and challenged scientists to a debate.
statements.counterpoint: Over 2,000 scientists from Indian research institutions signed a joint statement rejecting the remarks. Singh's senior colleague Prakash Javadekar publicly asked him not to dilute science.

statements.quote: Don't get into those maths. Those maths have never helped Einstein discover gravity.

statements.venue: Gobind Ballabh Pant Social Science Institute, Jhunsi, Allahabad
statements.neutral_title: On reported remarks about poverty and mindset
statements.quote_note: The meeting was closed to reporters and no recording or first-party transcript has been located. The viral English wording came from the host institute's first press note, not from an established recording of Gandhi's original words; the institute issued a materially different clarification the next day. The quote remains null rather than treating either press note as verbatim speech.
statements.claim: That the host institute's first press note attributed to Gandhi the view that poverty was a state of mind and did not mean scarcity of food, money or material things, while a next-day clarification said he had distinguished material poverty from a poverty of thought.
statements.context: No media were invited. The first institute note supplied the widely repeated English wording and linked it to self-confidence through a self-help-group example. The same institute then said the remark had been misrepresented and that Gandhi had recognised both material deprivation and a poverty of thought. Without a recording, the archive cannot responsibly choose the harsher wording as his established statement.
statements.counterpoint: Material deprivation remains central to standard poverty measurement. That does not settle what Gandhi said at this closed event: the only first-party descriptions conflict, so this entry is held from the ladder pending primary evidence.

statements.context: Made during the 2012 Punjab assembly campaign and repeated when challenged. The state government disputed it; Gandhi did not withdraw it.
statements.counterpoint: The figure inverts the statistic it came from. statements.neutral_title: On an attributed 'Magical Train' campaign promise
statements.quote: In 2014 when he was elected Modiji said India had been a slow 'passenger train' for seventy years after Independence and now under his guidance and rule the country would become a sleek and shining 'Magical Train' which is destined for 'Achhe Din'. statements.claim: That Narendra Modi had used the quoted passenger-train and 'Magical Train' analogy as a campaign promise before the 2014 election.
statements.context: Gandhi used the attribution to set up his own comparison of the government to a train driven toward disaster. The archive indexes only whether the earlier quotation he placed in Modi's mouth has a supporting record; it does not score the surrounding criticism.
statements.counterpoint: India Today's search of the available campaign record found Modi discussing bullet trains but no matching 'passenger train', 'Magical Train', or promised-journey quotation. A universal negative cannot be proved from an incomplete political archive, so the finding is 'no supporting record found', not 'fabricated'.
